To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

apostatic predation can maintain diversity within prey populations and among prey species and that apostatic predations leads to nonuniform distributions among prey along aspect gradients, which is the diversity wavelength of the system.

(1) the diversity wavelength is a function of the strength of predation and of prey evolution, but is insensitive to the degree of apostasy; and (2) the diversity wavelength can be much smaller than the intrinsic wavelength, which implies that prey species with different intrinsic wavelengths may coexist on a prey assemblage.

(a) the diversity wavelength can be estimated by considering the relative strengths of the different processes acting on the system, (b) the diversity wavelength is inversely related to prey diversity, and (c) the diversity wavelength increases as the number of prey species increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of apostatic predation on the maintenance and evolution of prey diversity.
the influence of predator-prey interactions on the maintenance of genetic and species diversity in prey populations.
the maintenance of diversity and its consequences in prey populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
predation can be a major factor in the maintenance of diversity in prey populations, but the details of the mechanism by which this is achieved are complex.

apostasy is not an important factor in determining diversity in natural systems, but that the possibility of apostasy in conjunction with other factors should be considered when studying diversity in natural populations.
the effects of apostasy on prey populations are complex, and depend on the particular circumstances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the maintenance of diversity in prey populations is enhanced when the prey are polymorphic, when there are many different prey species, when the prey have evolved a high level of apostasy, and when predators have a high level of behavioral plasticity.
predation may be an important factor in maintaining diversity within and among prey populations.

apostatic predation may lead to a variety of interesting and complex effects on prey populations and their distributions, and may play a significant role in determining the diversity of prey species in natural systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maintenance of aspect diversity in prey is a complex process that depends on a variety of factors including the relative rates at which prey evolve and predators learn.
the maintenance of diversity among prey species is possible in a system where predation is the only selective force.
the diversity of prey species can be influenced by predation in a manner that depends on the relative strengths of predation and prey evolution.
